summary: Corporate root CA removed during depot reimage causes MDM enrollment loop and SMB mount failures
description: Issue summary: Several devices removed from the depot for warranty repairs and reimaged using the updated corporate golden image (2026-03 release) are failing post-deploy. After first boot they repeatedly attempt MDM enrollment, fail, and then re-trigger reimage/playbook runs resulting in an enrollment loop. Simultaneously, previously-mounted corporate SMB shares fail to authenticate due to TLS failures referencing an untrusted root. Impact: ~12 devices in the US-WEST fleet are affected; users cannot complete checkpoint onboarding or access network file shares. Root cause hypothesis: a corporate root CA certificate that was intentionally removed from the image (part of an expiring intermediate rotation) is still required by on-device cached credentials or by SMB servers that have not rotated. The image removal step removed the CA from the local machine trust store but some backend services still present cert chains anchored to that CA, causing mutual TLS and SMB signing/auth failures and triggering the provisioning agent to retry enrollment. Environment: production fleet, us-west depot, golden image tag: redwood-golden-2026-03. Affected OS builds: Windows 11 22H2 (corp branch) and Ubuntu 22.04 LTS (corporate image).
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Take a device that previously had corporate root CA in machine trust (pre-2026-02 image). 2) Reimage from depot using redwood-golden-2026-03 (which omits the old root). 3) Boot and allow provisioning agent to run. 4) Observe MDM onboarding attempt fail with TLS trust errors and the agent re-queueing the image step. 5) Attempt to mount \\corp-smb\shared and observe TLS/certificate errors in network logs.
observed_behavior: Provisioning agent logs show repeated enrollment attempts with error: 'TLS handshake failed: untrusted_root (0x800b0109)'. Windows event logs note Schannel errors citing chain building issues. SMB client reports NT_STATUS_INVALID_PARAMETER with additional details referencing TLS failure. Device subsequently reports 'Pending reimage' in the depot UI and user sees repeated OOBE prompts.
expected_behavior: Devices should complete MDM enrollment on first boot and mount SMB shares using current corporate PKI without trust errors. Reimage should not trigger enrollment loops.
logs: Provisioning agent: /var/log/redwood/provisioner.log (excerpt): [2026-03-11T08:12:03Z] ERR enrollment: tls: certificate signed by unknown authority. Windows event: Schannel 36869 - A fatal error occurred while creating an SSL client credential. SMB client: smbclient -L //corp-smb -d shows TLS: chain validation failed, missing anchor CA.
investigation_notes: - Confirmed image build intentionally removed root 'Corp-Root-2014' per rotation plan. - Network team validated SMB servers in us-west still return chains anchored to Corp-Root-2014; they were not yet rebuilt with the new intermediate due to dependency on legacy devices. (see linked confluence). - Affected devices show cached machine account keys referencing old CA in local machine cert store (thumbprint matches archived CA). - Replaying a repro: adding the removed root back into the image prevents the enrollment loop and SMB mounts succeed. - Hypothesis: The provisioning agent treats TLS failures during enrollment as a catastrophic provisioning error and marks machine for reimage; no backoff or specific handling for CA-mismatch.
workarounds: Short-term: Manually push Corp-Root-2014 into the local machine trust store via remote script for affected devices (tested and validated on 4 devices). Alternative: update SMB server chains to the new CA (requires infra change) - infra has scheduled a partial rollout but not yet complete. Recommended immediate mitigation is targeted cert restore for impacted inventory while servers complete rotation.
next_steps: 1) Coordinate with Infra/Security to prioritize SMB server cert rotation in us-west (owner: Priya Sharma). 2) Create a one-off imaging patch that reintroduces the legacy root for the next 48 hours to avoid new reimage loops while rotation completes (owner: Liam O'Connor). 3) Add defensive handling in provisioning agent to treat enrollment TLS 'untrusted_root' as a non-destructive failure with backoff and clearer error to SRE (follow-up INT ticket). 4) Run a sweep script to detect devices with machine certs referencing deprecated anchors and add to remediation queue.
